name: Miles

global_influences.evidence: Miles began performing English-language rock/pop material (debut album Miles, 1982) before transitioning to Bangla songwriting; Shafin Ahmed's exposure to Western musical training in England is cited as a formative influence on the band's sound.
global_influences.source: Wikipedia Miles (band); Wikipedia Shafin/Hamin Ahmed pages

local_adaptation_notes: After releasing English-language material in the early 1980s, Miles pivoted to Bangla-language songwriting starting with Protisruti (1991), consciously blending Eastern melodic sensibilities with Western rock/pop arrangements — a deliberate strategy credited with helping the band cross over to mass Bangladeshi audiences while retaining international-caliber production.
sound_evolution_summary: Early period (1979–1980s): English-language rock/pop oriented toward international audiences, reflecting the band's origins performing covers and originals in Dhaka's expatriate/diplomatic circuit. Transitional/breakthrough period (1991–1999): shift to Bangla-language albums (Protisruti, Prottasha, Probaho) established Miles as a mainstream rock institution with widely popular Bangla rock anthems. Later period (2000s–2015): continued output (Proticchobi, 2015) with refined pop-rock production while maintaining the band's core melodic identity.
concert_culture_notes: Regarded as one of South Asia's most popular rock bands with an extensive international touring history, including performances across the Bangladeshi diaspora (UK, US, Middle East) and major domestic festival/stadium shows.
listener_community_notes: One of the most broadly cross-generational fan bases in Bangladeshi rock, spanning listeners who first encountered the band's English-language era and later generations who grew up with its Bangla-language hits.
